title: An Orca Killed a Great White Shark in Under 2 Minutes. Alone

scenes.text: An orca killed a great white shark in under two minutes.
It grabbed the shark by the fin, tore it off, and ate one thing: the liver.
A shark's liver can be a third of its body. Pure fat. The orca left the rest.
Two orcas, Port and Starboard, have done it since 2017. Nine great whites washed up, livers gone.
Now the great whites just leave. After that attack, they vanished from the bay for four months.

description:
In June 2023, a lone orca named Starboard killed a great white shark off Mossel Bay, South Africa, in under two minutes, the first solo orca kill of a great white ever documented.
Starboard and his partner Port have been hunting great whites since 2017, tearing out the oil-rich liver and leaving the rest; at least nine shark carcasses have washed ashore near Gansbaai missing their livers. Tagged sharks now flee the area when the pair shows up, sometimes for months.
Orca or great white: who's the real apex predator? Comment below.
first_comment: Port and Starboard are named after the kinks in their dorsal fins, which bend left and right. Why do you think the orcas only eat the liver and leave the rest?
